headline: Council approved $1.1 million for police cruisers and body cameras and $1.5 million to hire 14 firefighters.
summary: The council approved money from free cash for police cruisers and body cameras, and a $1.5 million appropriation to hire 14 firefighter recruits. It referred the FY2027 minimum residential factor to a November 10 public hearing and approved a change to the urban renewal plan for 278 Middlesex Street. A motion to cut $28,430 from a $180,430 technology transfer failed.
decisions: Approved the appointments of Jennifer Gilbo to the Community Preservation Commission and Timothy Hovey to the Zoning Board of Appeals, by roll call.
Asked the city manager to have departments work with community partners to find underused public space and ways to increase foot traffic downtown; approved.
Asked the city to provide information on the anticipated opening of Bicentennial Park on Jackson Street; approved.
Approved $1.1 million from free cash for police cruisers and body cameras, 7-3 by roll call.
Approved a $1.5 million supplemental appropriation to hire 14 firefighter recruits; approved by roll call.
Referred the question of a leaning tree at 38 Fox Street to the city manager and DPW for a report and recommendation; approved.
Asked the city manager to have the proper department review the on-ramp from Centerville to the Hunts Falls Rotary, including signage; approved.
Asked the city manager to have departments offer a public Flock camera demonstration with a question-and-answer session; approved.
Approved, 8-2 by roll call, a motion for the clerk to prepare the minutes of the executive session on Flock cameras for later review on release.
Approved a request for a letter to clearly state opposition to repurposing the ICC building into any type of shelter.
Asked the city manager for a report on the yearly cost of freezing property tax increases for seniors over 75 who have owned and lived in their home for more than 30 years; approved.
Referred the FY2027 minimum residential factor to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Approved, 10-0 by roll call, a request to change the urban renewal plan for 278 Middlesex Street.
Failed, 3-6, a motion to cut $28,430 from the technology transfer, reducing it to $152,000.
Approved, 7-2 by roll call, a $180,430 transfer from the PEG access fund for technology improvements.
Referred a property damage claim for a report and recommendation; approved.
discussion: Members asked why police cruisers and body cameras were not in the budget and whether free cash should pay for them. A motion to send the request to the Finance Subcommittee was withdrawn.
On fire staffing, members asked whether 14 new firefighters would cut overtime, which is budgeted at $4 million. The city manager said the effect would not be known until the new hires join.
Speakers and members discussed Flock license plate cameras. Speakers urged independent oversight and a technology board, and members asked for a public demonstration with questions.
Members said residents had heard the ICC building might become a homeless shelter, and the council voted to send a letter opposing that use.
Members discussed a property tax freeze for seniors over 75, noting its cost and whether taxes could be deferred until a sale instead.
